key_share_what: What happened: Google Antigravity's 5h and weekly caps do not scale proportionally — 2–3 heavy 5h blocks can exhaust 100% of the weekly quota. On top of that, the entire Gemini 4 family (Neon / Carbon / Hydrogen / Argon) suffers from intermittent prompt-cache drops (cache_read_tokens = 0), re-billing the whole context from scratch. Google expanded Neon's cache pool and reset quotas on Nov 20–21, 2026, yet shard routing, mid-session model/effort switches, and idle timeouts still trigger drops.
key_share_why: Why I use Gemini less: Long agent loops and multi-turn tool calls burn through the weekly cap unpredictably on Gemini; I rely on Claude Code / Codex for main daily work and keep Gemini for scoped tasks or high-CP spots.
key_share_tip: How to save quota when using it: Start a fresh session (or /compact) when switching tasks, and avoid changing models or thinking effort mid-conversation; when quota is tight, avoid fanning out multiple long-context subagents in parallel.
my_usage_note: Default to a single main-session loop with progressively loaded Skills (keeping prompt caches intact and avoiding lossy handoffs); daily drivers cannot be weak—check for blockers first if stuck, then raise effort or step up the model. Dispatch subagents only for heavy file reading, parallel exploration, or independent review.
plan_split:
When and how to dispatch subagents (keep work in the main loop with Skills when feasible; delegating does not guarantee quota savings. Fresh context by default; Claude fork shares prefix cache only with the same model inside its 5-minute cache TTL, and reviewer / security never fork):
Claude Code: Agent runs subagents in isolated context and returns summaries; designer uses the frontend-design skill.
Codex: spawn_agent dispatches parallel subagents (default_subagent_model stays gpt-6.2-sol).
Antigravity: invoke_subagent runs subagents in the background with a clean context.
